verses.1: The book of the origin of Jesus the Messiah, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
verses.2: Abraham fathered Isaac, Isaac fathered Jacob, Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers,
verses.3: Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar, Perez fathered Hezron, Hezron fathered Aram,
verses.4: Aram fathered Aminadab, Aminadab fathered Nahshon, Nahshon fathered Salmon,
verses.5: Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab, Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth, Obed fathered Jesse,
verses.6: Jesse fathered King David, David fathered Solomon by Uriah’s wife,
verses.7: Solomon fathered Rehoboam, Rehoboam fathered Abijah, Abijah fathered Asa,
verses.8: Asa fathered Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, Joram fathered Uzziah,
verses.9: Uzziah fathered Jotham, Jotham fathered Ahaz, Ahaz fathered Hezekiah,
verses.10: Hezekiah fathered Manasseh, Manasseh fathered Amon, Amon fathered Josiah,
verses.11: Josiah fathered Jehoiachin and his brothers, during the Babylonian exile.
verses.12: After the Babylonian exile, Jehoiachin fathered Shealtiel, Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel,
verses.13: Zerubbabel fathered Abiud, Abiud fathered Eliakim, Eliakim fathered Azor,
verses.14: Azor fathered Sadoc, Sadoc fathered Achim, Achim fathered Eliud,
verses.15: Eliud fathered Eleazar, Eleazar fathered Matthan, Matthan fathered Jacob,
verses.16: Jacob fathered Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus called the Messiah.
verses.17: Thus, all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations, from David to the Babylonian exile fourteen generations, and from the Babylonian exile to the Messiah fourteen generations.
verses.18: Now the origin of Jesus the Messiah was like this: when his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found to be pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
verses.19: Joseph her husband, being a righteous man and not wanting to expose her to disgrace, resolved to dismiss her quietly.
verses.20: But while he was considering this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
verses.21: She will bear a son, and you will name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.”
verses.22: All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had spoken through the prophet:
verses.23: “Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel,” which means “God is with us.”
verses.24: When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took his wife.
verses.25: And he did not know her until she gave birth to a son, and he named his name Jesus.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 16: “the husband of Mary” is a literal translation of “τὸν ἄνδρα Μαρίας,” which could also be “Mary’s husband,” but the former reads more clearly in English.  
- v. 23: “Emmanuel” is rendered according to the Greek, which translates the Hebrew as “God is with us.”

[1] The book of the origin of Jesus the Messiah, the son of David, the son of Abraham.  
[2] Abraham fathered Isaac, Isaac fathered Jacob, Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers,  
[3] Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar, Perez fathered Hezron, Hezron fathered Aram,  
[4] Aram fathered Aminadab, Aminadab fathered Nahshon, Nahshon fathered Salmon,  
[5] Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab, Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth, Obed fathered Jesse,  
[6] Jesse fathered King David, David fathered Solomon by Uriah’s wife,  
[7] Solomon fathered Rehoboam, Rehoboam fathered Abijah, Abijah fathered Asa,  
[8] Asa fathered Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, Joram fathered Uzziah,  
[9] Uzziah fathered Jotham, Jotham fathered Ahaz, Ahaz fathered Hezekiah,  
[10] Hezekiah fathered Manasseh, Manasseh fathered Amon, Amon fathered Josiah,  
[11] Josiah fathered Jehoiachin and his brothers, during the Babylonian exile.  
[12] After the Babylonian exile, Jehoiachin fathered Shealtiel, Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel,  
[13] Zerubbabel fathered Abiud, Abiud fathered Eliakim, Eliakim fathered Azor,  
[14] Azor fathered Sadoc, Sadoc fathered Achim, Achim fathered Eliud,  
[15] Eliud fathered Eleazar, Eleazar fathered Matthan, Matthan fathered Jacob,  
[16] Jacob fathered Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus called the Messiah.  
[17] Thus, all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations, from David to the Babylonian exile fourteen generations, and from the Babylonian exile to the Messiah fourteen generations.  
[18] Now the origin of Jesus the Messiah was like this: when his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found to be pregnant by the Holy Spirit.  
[19] Joseph her husband, being a righteous man and not wanting to expose her to disgrace, resolved to dismiss her quietly.  
[20] But while he was considering this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.  
[21] She will bear a son, and you will name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.”  
[22] All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had spoken through the prophet:  
[23] “Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel,” which means “God is with us.”  
[24] When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took his wife.  
[25] And he did not know her until she gave birth to a son, and he named his name Jesus.

Notes  
- v. 16: “the husband of Mary” is a literal translation of “τὸν ἄνδρα Μαρίας,” which could also be “Mary’s husband,” but the former reads more clearly in English.  
- v. 23: “Emmanuel” is rendered according to the Greek, which translates the Hebrew as “God is with us.”
